Three of the 10 most expensive signings in the history of football have happened this summer – with all of them being Premier League signings. In fact, this summer window featured four of the top flight's five most expensive ever deals.

Fernandez was the headline move, surpassing the £116m Manchester City spent earlier in the window to sign Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, while Chelsea paid £117m to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Meanwhile, Liverpool paid an initial £106m, which could rise to £123m, for Paris St-Germain and France forward Bradley Barcola.

Yan Diomande's move to Real Madrid and Anthony Gordon's switch from Newcastle to Barcelona are the only deals completed so far this summer by clubs outside the Premier League to involve fees in excess of £60m.

Tottenham's acquisition of Sandro Tonali was a club-record fee which could reach £100m, while the north London club have also spent heavily on Mateus Fernandes (£85m) from West Ham and Savio from Manchester City (£75m potentially rising to £85m).

Other transfers around this range include the £85.6m deal that City struck to bring in Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, Bruno Guimaraes' arrival at Arsenal for £75m from Newcastle, and Manchester United landing Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton for £70m.

So maybe it is not surprising then that in the compilation of the 20 most expensive transfers completed that only six were not to clubs in the English top flight.

Indeed, newly-promoted Ipswich Town have spent more on new signings than the likes of Barcelona, AC Milan, Juventus and reigning European champions PSG.

Manchester City's late confirmation of the signing of Fernandez took their summer spending to £458m as new boss Enzo Maresca was well backed as he looks to build his own team after replacing Pep Guardiola.

That is a new Premier League record for a single transfer window, passing Liverpool's £415m from last summer. While City did spend big, they also made £304m in player sales.

Chelsea were the next biggest spenders as they paid out a total of £349m, although the Blues also sold £382m worth of players to end up with a net profit of £33m.

Tottenham spent the third-highest amount in the summer window with £302m as they hope to avoid another season of struggle and get back to battling at the top end of the table.

Newly-promoted Ipswich spent big in their bid to avoid an immediate return to the Championship with an overall outlay of £171m, outspending Manchester United, who paid out £148m on new signings.

Meanwhile, Hull - also back in the Premier League this season - had a very busy window with a total of 18 new additions, six of them arriving on deadline day.

Premier League clubs as a whole were willing to dip deep into their pockets this summer, as 11 of the 20 clubs broke their transfer records, six of them on more than one occasion.

Coventry, promoted to the Premier League alongside Ipswich and Hull, have done so four times over.

They signed Aurele Amenda for an initial £15.4m, before that fee was surpassed by £20m for Loum Tchaouna. Goalkeeper Carl Rushworth made his loan move permanent for £22m but Caleb Yirenkyi now holds the club record after he signed for £23.1m.

Aston Villa and Ipswich also broke their respective records more than once, while James Trafford (Leeds), Mamadou Sangare (Brentford), Luka Vuskovic (Brighton) and Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest) were all £40m-plus club-record buys.

This summer, 35% of deals involving a transfer fee have been from one Premier League club to another, which is an increase from last year, when the figure was 30%.

That then increases to 44% in instances where Premier League clubs have bought players from lower down the English football pyramid.

On top of that, the Premier League net spend remains over £1bn for this window - by far the most in Europe - despite many of the biggest sales this summer coming from the English league too. Bundesliga and Ligue 1 clubs have received 

Aside from French-based duo Barcola and Bouaddi, the majority of major signings made by Premier League clubs this month have been from rival clubs in the same division.

They include England team-mates Rogers and Anderson, while Newcastle sold Tonali to Spurs and Guimaraes to Arsenal.

Manchester United snapped up Baleba from Brighton after a 12-month chase to aid their midfield revamp, while Tottenham's recruitment of Fernandes and Savio is in the same category.

But why are English clubs buying each other's players more than ever this summer instead of shopping abroad for the biggest deals?

One reason could be the temptation for players who are proven in the Premier League.

Many of last season's big-money signings - with a good chunk of them coming from the Bundesliga - failed to meet expectations or justify their transfer fee.

There have also been deals this summer involving the same clubs, possibly with accounting in mind, with Chelsea and Villa selling players to each other.

And there is also a feeling that teams abroad increase the transfer fees they are asking for when English teams - with all their TV riches - show interest in their players.

title: Barcelona new signing compares La Liga with the Premier League – ‘Football here is different’
description: Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assis...
fullText:
Anthony Gordon produced a stellar performance in the final third as Barcelona secured a comprehensive 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night.

The summer signing from Newcastle United notably assisted one of the goals from Raphinha while also playing a crucial role in Florian Lejeune's own goal.

The Englishman demonstrated excellent chemistry with his teammates and appears to be settling in well in La Liga.

In the wake of his performance against Rayo, the forward tried to compare La Liga's brand of football with the Premier League.

Gordon acknowledged the intensity of English football but highlighted the different demands of Spanish football.

"I'm not going to deny that the Premier League is incredibly intense. The rhythm is relentless, there are physical battles everywhere, long band kicks, corner kicks and a lot of contact.

Gordon had an outstanding game vs Rayo. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"That's why many English players believe it is the best league in the world. They're used to that kind of chaos," he said, as quoted by SPORT.

The Englishman then pointed out the nuances of Spanish football, especially in relation to the recent game against Rayo Vallecano.

"Football in Spain is different. Rayo retreated and tried to make the match difficult, something you also see in many mid-table Premier League teams. The difference is that we don't just resort to long balls or relying on ball-to-ball plays," he said.

Gordon praised Barcelona's style as the key differentiator, saying: "We moved the ball, Pedri found spaces between the lines, Lamine and the others created numerical superiority and patiently disarmed them with our football."

The forward also flagged the technical precision required in La Liga, as he said:

"In England, sometimes intensity can cover up mistakes. You can mis-control the ball and still recover by winning the next physical battle. Here, a bad first touch or a lack of concentration on your positioning can punish you immediately."

"The spaces are smaller, the decisions have to be faster and everything must be cleaner," he added.

Gordon's cross forced Lejeune's own goal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Gordon believes the Spanish game actually enhances one of his biggest strengths.

"My speed becomes even more effective here because the movement around me creates opportunities and spaces, rather than everyone simply running forward in straight lines," he said.

At the same time, though, the Englishman was careful not to disrespect the league in which he grew up.

"I loved playing in the Premier League and it played a huge role in my development. But Spanish football demands a different level of tactical and technical intelligence," he said.

He did, however, offer an observation about how certain English sides would cope.

"Some Premier League teams would have a hard time playing this style consistently because they may not have the patience or quality in the midfield that is required."

"That's not disrespecting them, it's just what I've noticed in my first games. There's a different football intelligence here," Gordon concluded.

title: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
description: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
fullText:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City): Again, another massive performance, another clean sheet. Hull have taken everyone by surprise, but it's because of that defensive shape and defensive organisation, and obviously, he is at the heart of that as well.

Semi Ajayi (Hull City): Coming up with Hull is the only way he was going to ever play in the Premier League. He has been doing the rounds in the Championship for years. A real good solid pro. He has taken this opportunity and he's been an absolute beast, so fair play to him.

Nordi Mukiele (Sunderland): He was great last season, a real, real powerful centre-half. Again, a top performance from him. Fulham had no shots on target - he was a massive part of that.

James Tarkowski (Everton): It was a captain's performance for Everton. Just one of those guys that you want in your team. No-one ever respects him, no-one ever rates him, but when you play against him and when he's in your team, he's a real bloke. Proper captain, proper leader of men, and kept going right to the end. And ultimately, even though the two Bournemouth defenders decided to mark themselves, he was the one who got the goal.

James McAtee (Nottingham Forest): He absolutely ran the game at Anfield from start to finish. Getting on the ball in the pockets, half-turn, playing forward. He was the reason they were any good, and he's very, very good, but won't be spoken about in the same breath as the goalscorers.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United): There's not much more to say. Captain Fantastic, three goals, an assist, and nearly scored from the halfway line. Where would Manchester United be without him? Relegated is the answer.

Rayan Cherki (Manchester City): My favourite player in world football to watch. Amazing the way he's gifted with the ball, the way he manipulates the ball, and also the way he's able to think for himself. And I just like the fact he's carefree. He just wants to play football, so that's great.

Anthony Elanga (Newcastle): Back-to-back weeks, another great goal, another great performance. Just looks like he's had another lease of life under this manager. And I wonder whether we're going to see the Elanga that we saw at Nottingham Forest, just terrorising defences with that pace. But also, before he even gets there, they're just worried about what he can do.

Yoane Wissa (Newcastle): I had to shoehorn him in because ultimately he's been great through the middle, but the two strikers have actually scored more and played better than him. But Wissa's a massive part of why Newcastle have done well, although he's not being talked about enough in terms of the application that he puts in. So much so, that Woltemade could be sold. That's how much of a good job Wissa has done.

Joao Pedro (Chelsea): He has had an unbelievable start to the season. I think under Xabi Alonso, and with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers behind him, he's going to have an unbelievable season. But also the fact that he wasn't even picked for the World Cup. Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti was there, and Joao Pedro looks like he has a point to prove.

Erling Haaland (Manchester City): The beast, the Viking, the new haircut. Two goals, comfortable. Just looks like actually playing football is too easy for him. He looks like scoring goals is just becoming a bit boring and he's probably trying to think of ways to do it better.

Matthias Jaissle (Newcastle): What a start to the season he's had. Also, the demeanour he gives off is young Jose Mourinho vibes. Very Jose at Porto, without saying he's the Special One. Calm, confident, a little bit arrogant at times, but also just looks like you want to play for him. Looks like he knows what he's talking about.

title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: What Arteta and Saka said
description: Saka scored in consecutive Premier League appearances for the first time since November 2024, with all three of his goals in the competition against Villa coming at Villa Park.  Arsenal have now started their Premier League season with two wins in a row for the seventh time in the last eight seasons, including the last five in a row.
fullText:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta speaking to Match of the Day: "This is a really difficult place to come and win the game. Last season we lost in the last kick of the game. They were hurt after what happened last week. It was a great squad performance tonight."

On if this is his best team in terms of strength in depth: "That is what we need. The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum.

"The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season."

Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka, speaking to Sky Sports: "Very, very tough game. It's not easy coming here, they made it hard for us. It feels even better to come out with the win.

"The way they defend, really compact and with a high line, they caught us offside. We had to adapt to that. Different from what we faced last week, we weren't able to implement our attacking pattern.

"One goal is normally enough for us because we are so solid at the back. When we got the first one, it actually opened the game up. We wanted to push for the second one.

"All the full-backs, the way they play gives us a lot. For us wingers, it opens up the game for us, we've always got composure in the box.

"We weren't at our highest level with the ball. Without it, we were incredible. As soon as we lost it, we were running back. We knew that they liked to play in transition.

"All the boys put in a shift tonight. It helps with a clean sheet."

Saka scored in consecutive Premier League appearances for the first time since November 2024, with all three of his goals in the competition against Villa coming at Villa Park.

Arsenal have now started their Premier League season with two wins in a row for the seventh time in the last eight seasons, including the last five in a row.

title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: What Emery said
description: Aston Villa have lost their first two Premier League matches of the season for the first time since 2019-20.  Since Opta began recording shot data in 2003-04, Aston Villa are just the second team to fail to have a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season, along with Swansea City in 2017-18 who were later relegated that season.
fullText:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, speaking to Match of the Day: "We performed like we planned and we competed like we planned. We didn't achieve the result, of course, it's painful. But through how we played and competed, that is the way we want to build again, to build a team like we want. The debut of some players was fantastic."

On if is excited to work with new players: "We are happy how we are closing the transfer window. We are not regretting anything. The players we have joining should be enough to build the team again with the structure we want."

On Taylor Harwood-Bellis watching in the stands: "I don't know if it's official, hopefully we can close everything. We did a fantastic job in the last three years, now with the new chapter, try to rebuild the team as fast as possible."

On last year's success despite a slow start and if people are quick to forget that: "Each year is different. We have an idea in our mind to build again and create a new chapter. We have lost two matches. We don't want to compare with the past, we must focus on this year."

Aston Villa have lost their first two Premier League matches of the season for the first time since 2019-20. They are the first team to finish in the top-four of the top-flight (4th in 2025-26) and then lose their first two games of the following season since both Arsenal and Manchester United in 1992-93, and first to do so without scoring since QPR in 1976-77.

Since Opta began recording shot data in 2003-04, Aston Villa are just the second team to fail to have a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season, along with Swansea City in 2017-18 who were later relegated that season.

title: Man Utd pay tribute to 'proud Red' officer who died in A66 crash
description: The widow and two children of PC Matthew Blades will be at Old Trafford for Manchester United's Premier League game with Ipswich.
fullText:
The two sons of a police officer killed in a crash on Teesside will lead out the Manchester United team as mascots for Sunday's Premier League match against Ipswich at Old Trafford.

PC Matthew Blades, described as a "proud Red" by United, was a regular at Old Trafford. The club have paid tribute to him in Sunday's match programme. His widow will attend the game with their children.

PC Blades and his colleague PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

United said they learned of the deaths of the two officers "with great sadness".

"Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others," said the club, in a tribute in the programme.

At Elland Road, match officials for Leeds United's Premier League fixture against Brentford on Sunday wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades.

On Saturday, there was a minute's applause in memory of PC Blades and PC Clough before Middlesbrough's Championship encounter with West Brom at Riverside Stadium. Pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Earlier this week, 17 people were arrested in connection with the investigation into the crash bringing the total number of arrests to 24.

The occupants of the other vehicle, a Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17, also died.

fullText:
Liverpool view Cody Gakpo as a proven multi-functional Premier League attacker and he has shown that with a goal and an assist in their first two games this season.

But all summer, the understanding has been that if the club bring in the attacking players they want, they would not stand in the way of Gakpo if a solid offer came in.

Given how late in the transfer window the talks are taking place between Liverpool and Manchester City, the Anfield side will now consider the situation before sanctioning any move.

Liverpool are also hoping to bring in another winger before deadline day.

With the arrival of Victor Munoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola's imminent move from PSG, Gakpo is well aware that he may not be first choice any more, so if a move does happen it would not come as a surprise.

Financially it will be a great outcome for Liverpool if they agree a deal for about £85m given they signed Gakpo for £35m from PSV Eindhoven after the World Cup in 2022.

But with Hugo Ekitike missing until 2027 with a ruptured Achilles tendon, and Alexander Isak's injury struggles, they would be taking a massive risk letting Gakpo leave.

title: Antonio helps young Ghanaians chase Premier League dreams
description: Former West Ham forward Michail Antonio is helping players from a Ghana academy, who have travelled to England in the hope of turning pro.
fullText:
In the heat of rural Leicestershire, the Samba Stars are chasing their dream.

Head coach Freddie Okyere has just finished a shooting exercise and allows the squad to catch their breath.

The teenagers from the Ghanaian academy, which is backed by former West Ham and Nottingham Forest forward Michail Antonio, have spent two and a half months in England with one goal - impressing clubs and earning a contract.

While scouts do visit west Africa, it is rare for academies to travel to the UK to put their players directly in front of professional clubs.

"The talent the lads have is incredible," said Antonio.

"We created Samba Stars Academy to give young players in Ghana access to elite coaching, shape them as players and create real avenues into the pro game and show how much talent Ghana has."

Based in Kumasi while building a new facility in Bompata, just over 100 miles north of Ghana's capital Accra, the Samba Stars' tactic has paid off.

Bournemouth, Everton, Manchester City, Charlton, Preston, Barnsley and Peterborough have all taken players on trial this summer.

"The first two or three weeks it hadn't sunk in, but then they saw the facilities we'd be [using] and the teams we were playing," said Okyere.

"They want to go and show what they can do. They are hungry, they really want it. I'm hoping there will be so much interest because we have so much talent here.

"With the facilities we will have in Ghana we feel we will be top two, top three [academies]. We hope we can bring the best of Ghana to Europe."

There are other success stories, with midfielder Listowell Lord Hinneh joining Middlesbrough in February after a trial., external

The 18-year-old has trained with the first team after swapping west Africa for England's north east.

"When I came in January, it was so cold. Experiencing something like that for the first time was tough," he told BBC Sport.

"Moving was a big milestone. It just makes me feel the dreams I've been having, thinking of trying to find myself in Europe to become a professional footballer.

"I feel the kind of dreams that I want, I'm on the verge. I'm on the way [to] becoming who I wanted to become."

Hinneh - whose sister Groovy lives in Leeds - met with the Samba Stars squad on their trip, offering advice.

"[I told them] what you've been dreaming about the future, it starts from here," he said.

"Don't just try, be so passionate. You need to play and enjoy it because you can have the success in whatever you're doing. You have to just put your heart in it."

All but one of the 20-strong visiting group initially had their visa application denied before eventually being admitted after re-evaluation.

Since arriving in the UK, they have been hosted by Brook House College in Market Harborough and trained at Harborough Town, who play in the National League North.

"The football [here] is very detailed," said 17-year-old goalkeeper Joshua Tetteh Tuwor.

"In Ghana we have the same passion but I'm seeing a different side of professional football.

"We are grateful to have such opportunities to train with elite coaches."

Rob Newman, formerly West Ham's head of recruitment and Manchester City's international scouting and recruitment manager, spent time with the academy in Ghana earlier this year and has helped coach them in Harborough.

"Hopefully clubs can see the potential," said the ex-Bristol City and Norwich defender.

"Nothing will give me greater pleasure in six months [than] going to see these boys playing in a first team in Europe. I believe they are two or three months away from being able to do that."

The Stars have played a series of games against youth teams from the EFL and non-league.

They started with a 9-0 thumping of Dorking Wanderers and also beat Under-21 sides from Sheffield Wednesday, Luton and Peterborough.

There were draws at Sheffield United and Barnsley while their only defeat came 3-2 against Preston's U21s.

Antonio watched them thrash Peterborough U19s 6-0 last month.

"You can see from what they've done since they've been in the UK - the results against top teams - that they have what it takes to play pro level," said the 36-year-old.

"It's great to help knock down barriers and give these lads a real chance."

Ghana have reached five of the past six Fifa World Cups - having never qualified before 2006 - and made the quarter-finals in 2010.

At this year's tournament, where they exited in the last-32 against Colombia, eight members of the squad were born overseas.

The Black Stars may not have come to rely heavily on diaspora talent, unlike some other African nations, yet the Ghana Football Association has made noises about widening its global search - something which could potentially impact home-grown talent.

"You have to have a tough mentality," said Sherif Mashud, an 18-year-old striker who has already had a trial with Hungarian top-tier side Zalaegerszegi thanks to his involvement with Samba Stars.

"Back home everyone is depending on you, everyone is looking up to you to succeed, to come and help them, your friends, your family. Everyone is praying for you."

The new English season has begun with six Ghana internationals on Premier League books: Mohammed Kudus at Tottenham, Antoine Semenyo with Manchester City, Brighton's Ibrahim Osman, Ipswich's new signing Abdul Fatawu and Coventry's Brandon Thomas-Asante and Caleb Yirenkyi.

The first to play in the English top flight was striker Nii Lamptey when he joined Aston Villa in 1994, while midfielder Michael Essien has made the most appearances, winning two titles with Chelsea.

Only two other Ghanaians have lifted the Premier League trophy - Jeffrey Schlupp and Daniel Amartey when Leicester stunned the world in 2015-16.

"Back home we've got people you grew up with and you might miss them, but that doesn't kill the dreams I'm here for," said Hinneh, who lists Kudus as his biggest inspiration and hopes to follow his heroes into the top flight after Boro missed out on promotion in last season's Championship play-off final.

"I'm trying to figure out what the reality is, what the future holds for me and then just chase the dreams."

title: Martinez is eighth Chelsea-Villa deal in four years
description: After Emiliano Martinez's move, BBC Sport looks at why Aston Villa and Chelsea have become one of the Premier League’s busiest transfer partnerships since 2022.
fullText:
Chelsea have signed Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa for £7.5m - the eighth deal between the two clubs in the past four years.

The 33-year-old, who won the World Cup in 2022, has moved to Stamford Bridge on a three-year deal.

Former Arsenal goalkeeper Martinez joined Villa in 2020 and made 256 appearances, helping the club win the Europa League last season.

"I'm delighted to be at this football club," Martinez said.

"Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I'm just over the moon - I can't wait to get started.

'I want to be successful here. I'm someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it's a football club that wins titles, so I think it's a good match."

Martinez's move to Chelsea comes after Nicolas Jackson's transfer the other way last week.

No two Premier League clubs have exchanged more players, on permanent or loan deals, in the past four years.

The relationship began after Chelsea's owners, BlueCo, took control of the club in 2022 and signed Carney Chukwuemeka from Villa for £20m that summer. Ian Maatsen (£37.5m, to Villa), Omari Kellyman (£19m, to Chelsea) and Axel Disasi (a £5m loan deal, to Villa) subsequently moved between the clubs.

This summer alone has brought four more deals. Morgan Rogers completed a £117m move Chelsea, while Alejandro Garnacho joined Villa on loan with a conditional obligation to buy in a deal worth around £43m.

Jackson then moved to Villa for £65m, before Martinez followed.

Since 2022, Chelsea have paid Aston Villa £163.5m for players. Villa have spent £102.5m on Chelsea players including Axel Disasi's loan fee. That figure could rise to £150.5m should certain criteria be met to make Garnacho's loan move permanent. Chelsea believe the terms are easily reachable.

Chelsea and Villa have done business before. Tammy Abraham, Ross Barkley, Danny Drinkwater, Ryan Bertrand, Steve Sidwell and Andy Townsend are among those to have moved between the clubs during the Premier League era, while John Terry joined Villa after leaving Chelsea.

But the recent volume of business between the clubs has not gone unnoticed elsewhere in the Premier League, at a time when both have had to navigate domestic and European financial regulations. One source told BBC Sport that a number of club executives have raised questions about the frequency of the dealings.

There is no suggestion, though, that either club have broken any rules.

BBC Sport has approached Chelsea and Aston Villa for comment.

BBC Sport has counted every permanent transfer and loan between Premier League clubs since the summer of 2022, restricting the analysis to the 15 sides who have been in the top flight throughout that period.

There is a tie at the top: Chelsea have done eight deals with Villa, and another eight with Brighton.

Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest are next on six, followed by Arsenal and Chelsea on five.

Chelsea feature in six of the 10 busiest club pairings, illustrating the scale of their player trading since the BlueCo consortium completed its takeover.

BlueCo's £4.25bn purchase of Chelsea ended Roman Abramovich's 19-year ownership and ushered in a period of significant squad turnover.

But Villa's close relationship with Chelsea also has a more specific explanation.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Villa owner Nassef Sawiris have developed a close working relationship and have communicated directly over transfer business.

That relationship has spanned several transfer windows and included Rogers' move to Stamford Bridge this summer.

Chelsea did not have a clear run at Rogers, though - as Arsenal also wanted to sign him, and it was the player's decision to move to Stamford Bridge.

Uefa has the power to scrutinise transfers completed between the same clubs within a 45-day period. Garnacho's move to Villa - on an initial loan deal - came two days after Rogers signed for Chelsea. Jackson's permanent transfer went through 38 days after the Rogers one.

But a timeline on its own is not evidence that the deals were in any way related.

Villa, for instance, could point to their long-held interest in Jackson, who previously worked with head coach Unai Emery at Villarreal.

Chelsea, meanwhile, could argue their interest in Martinez was independent of previous dealings with Villa and would have been pursued regardless of the club he played for. The goalkeeper had attracted interest from Juventus earlier in the window, with a finger injury understood to have scuppered a move.

There are broader reasons why domestic transfers remain attractive, but money is often the biggest factor.

Premier League clubs generally have greater spending power than most teams elsewhere in Europe, meaning another English side may be among the few buyers capable of meeting the fee and wage demands of a selling club.

That can make domestic deals particularly attractive when clubs are trying to move on high-value players. Signing from within the league also reduces some of the uncertainty, with recruitment teams already familiar with a player's qualities and performances.

Yet even in a league where domestic trading is commonplace, the frequency of deals between Villa and Chelsea stands out.

title: 'Not bad for the worst team in Premier League history' - Hull's perfect start
description: Hull striker Oli McBurnie has a playful dig at his team's critics after beating Coventry to win their opening two Premier League games.
fullText:
"To say we're the worst team in Premier League history, it's not a bad start from the boys," said Ollie McBurnie, in a light-hearted jab to Hull's critics.

Liam Millar's late winner at Coventry made it two wins from two to leave the Tigers in dreamland on their Premier League return.

After the opening day victory over Manchester United it was a different, gritty, display on Saturday but winning at CBS Arena, against a perceived relegation rival, earns Hull huge momentum and belief.

"We don't feel we have anything to prove to anyone. No-one has given us the Premier League, we have all earned it," said striker McBurnie.

"We're there on merit, we deserve to be there, we don't have anything to prove to anyone. It's been a great start."

The Scotland international refused to get carried away but the tune of "we're going to win the league" from the away end signalled the Hull fans' glee.

It may be fanciful but at least history is on the Tigers' side as they look to stay in the division.

Only three teams have ever been relegated from the top flight having won their first two games.

One was the Tigers themselves in 2016-17. Wolves in 2011-12 and West Brom in 2017-18 are the others.

Their Premier League survival chances were written off instantly after beating Middlesbrough in the Championship play-off final last season. They now sit second in the early table.

At Coventry, Hull looked built for the Premier League. Hulking defender Semi Ajayi dominated at the heart of the Tigers' defence to limit the Sky Blues, who ultimately ran out of ideas.

Nobel Mendy and Lucas Gourna-Douath towered above the hosts while McBurnie was a constant nuisance.

The Tigers are the first promoted side to win their opening two games for nine years, since Huddersfield dispatched Crystal Palace and Newcastle.

The Terriers beat the drop by four points in 2017-18 and that remains the goal for boss Sergej Jakirovic, especially after his men struggled to find inspiration at Coventry until Millar's intervention.

Prior to the substitute's winner there was frustration pouring out of Mendy when Hull's record signing threw his hands in the air and pulled his shirt over his head after being withdrawn on the hour.

The Sky Blues had almost 70% possession but were unable to break Hull down - and as Coventry's agitation grew so did the Tigers' belief.

"The longer the game was 0-0 the pressure was more on them to win the game. A draw was not a bad result for us," added McBurnie.

For Coventry, after 25 years away it was not supposed to start like this.

All the anticipation, all the waiting and it ends with a crushing dose of reality.

A second successive defeat will serve as a reminder that, despite the euphoria of their top-flight return, this season will be a constant battle.

Coventry can at least seek solace in the fact 10 promoted sides have lost their first two Premier League games and survived, the last being Aston Villa in 2019-20.

But they will need to improve. Having scored 97 goals in winning the title last season they must rediscover that touch, although they are not helped by Haji Wright's thigh injury which will keep him sidelined for weeks.

When the fixtures came out, though, a home game with fellow promoted side Hull stood out as one to get early points.

Sandwiched between an opener at champions Arsenal and a trip to runners-up Manchester City the Sky Blues needed to take something.

Yet owner Doug King looked on grimly from the stands as he watched time tick by and the Sky Blues fail to recover from Millar's 82nd-minute strike.

The opening 3-0 defeat at Arsenal was understandable but this defeat leaves them already playing catch up.

They were persistent but limited, with seven of the starting XI remaining from the 0-0 draw against Hull which opened last season's Championship campaign.

There was a nervousness about the Sky Blues, which was picked up by boss Frank Lampard. It is something which needs eradicating quickly.

"This season was always going to be very different to last season but I sensed a bit of edge, that quality of pass and playing safe rather than play forward," he said. "Maybe that is apprehension.

"I don't like the excuse of it. Last week that was valid because of the level of opposition, the occasion, 25 years out and a lot of debuts. We shouldn't use it as an excuse today.

"It's a game against a team we played twice last year and we finished a lot of points above them. The Premier League gives that edge and we will have to get used to that and quickly.

"The lesson is don't expect anything in the Premier League. It depends how much you want it to be (a mental blow). There are 36 games left, we're two games in. It depends how you want to react to defeats."

Ashley Williams believes the defeat will hit Coventry's confidence.

The former Wales captain won promotion to the Premier League with Swansea in 2011 and knows how crucial the early psychological blows can be.

"They blitzed the Championship last year and were full of confidence coming into the season. But after two defeats everything suddenly becomes that much harder," he said on the BBC's Final Score programme.

"As players, you look at the table and it's not nice when you are at the wrong end of it. Straight away they'll see they are already six points behind Hull and that's a real kick in the teeth.

"All those little doubts start to kick in so they've got to get to work and figure it out fast and I'm sure Frank Lampard will do that. However, Manchester City away next up is far from ideal."

title: £300m spent, bottom of the table... but Spurs boss De Zerbi 'not angry'
description: Having spent more than £300m in the summer, Tottenham find themselves bottom of the Premier League, without a point or a goal, but boss Roberto de Zerbi remains optimistic.
fullText:
Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi said he was "not angry" and there was "no panic" after his side's second loss in two games left them bottom of the Premier League – but it was a depressingly familiar story for the club's fans.

Goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa in a 10-minute second-half spell gave Newcastle a 2-0 victory, with thousands of Spurs supporters heading for the exits early.

They have every reason to be annoyed as they have now seen only three home league wins from their past 23 matches at their superb stadium.

Seventeenth in the Premier League in 2024-25, 17th in 2025-26, only avoiding relegation on the final day, but this season was meant to be different.

With more than £300m spent in the summer, Spurs fans were expecting a push to get back into Europe, having won the Europa League two seasons ago and been in the last 16 of the Champions League in March.

Instead, in the Premier League it is played two, lost two, scored none, 20th out of 20.

"We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result," said De Zerbi.

"Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded, we played better than Newcastle.

"We are disappointed for the result and [for] our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team, we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham."

After beating Everton on the final day of last season to stay up, Tottenham tried to ensure they were not in a relegation scrap this year.

In came midfielders Mateus Fernandes from West Ham and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £85m and £100m respectively, defender Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52m and Manchester City winger Savio, formerly known as Savinho, for £75m, although he missed Saturday's match because of "muscle fatigue".

Defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, plus goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, have arrived on free transfers and striker Omar Marmoush made his debut against Newcastle following his loan from Manchester City, with the deal becoming a permanent £60m transfer next summer.

After a 3-0 loss at Brentford last week, more home pain was inflicted on the Spurs support, although the Magpies scored with both of their attempts on target as Tottenham failed to convert any of their 17 attempts, six of which were on target.

"Forget the result," insisted De Zerbi. "I am not angry, we are working well and were unlucky today with the result.

"There is no panic. I know where we are going and what the plan is. I'm sorry for the fans for the result. We have to improve. We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection between the players."

Former Tottenham and England goalkeeper Joe Hart was not as positive about Spurs' performances and said: "The frustration in the stadium, and among the fans, will be they are looking at that Spurs team and wondering what they are trying to achieve.

"When you see a Newcastle side who have been through massive change over the summer - and a more difficult change than Spurs have - it's hard as in two games you can clearly see what [Newcastle boss] Matthias Jaissle is trying to do. The players are on board with it and they are flying.

"The concern for Tottenham is they can't say the same. But there's been a lot of change and it's not easy to bed in that many players under so much pressure.

"Hardly anyone has been able to find the remedy at the club so it's not like it's an easy fix. They've not just suddenly fallen off a cliff, they've been struggling in the league for a while.

"Roberto de Zerbi needs to get his new players to settle in quickly as the Premier League comes at you so fast, and it feels like his team are second-guessing everything at the moment."

Former England goalkeeper Rob Green, speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, added: "Lukas Hornicek made some saves in the first half but Tottenham were short of invention, creation, goals.

"For Tottenham, the same questions last season are still here this season. Performances like this will indicate that they need a vast improvement from this set of players that have come into this club.

"They will need the characters as much as anything to turn this around. It doesn't take much for these Spurs fans to turn and the belief start to drain from the players."

The transfer window closes on Tuesday, and on Friday De Zerbi said he was still seeking "one player 

After the Newcastle match he was asked about the potential departures of Kevin Danso, Pape Matar Sarr and Richarlison, who have all been linked with moves away from Tottenham.

"I have very good relationships but if they want to leave, they have to bring the solution, the economic solution, to the club, and they can go," he said.

De Zerbi was only appointed at the end of March, earning 11 points in seven matches to keep Spurs up, and insists it will not be a quick fix to the club's problems.

"We have to improve and to change two seasons like the last two is impossible in 10 days and with people in the transfer market," said the Italian.

"We have to work hard on the pitch and find the connection with the players because last season before the end of the season we were in the Championship and we stayed up together.

"Now we have to keep calm and focus on improvement. We have a great squad and great players."

title: How overlooked Liverpool signing can pave the way forward in post-Salah era
description: Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest: Iraola and Glasner remain winless in the Premier League but the Reds came from behind twice to nick a point
fullText:
Wingers come in different guises and at different prices. On the day Liverpool agreed to pay up to £123m for Bradley Barcola, the man signed for rather less, and with rather less fanfare, again spared Andoni Iraola a first defeat of his reign. On Sunday at Newcastle, Victor Munoz won the penalty that produced Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th-minute equaliser. On his Anfield bow, the £34m Spaniard delivered a devastating equaliser.

That both contributions came from the right flank, though he had started on the left against Nottingham Forest, may be pertinent. The presumption is that Barcola will be used on the left. While Liverpool are yet to replace Mohamed Salah, they got two equalisers from the men stationed in his old spot here, with Cody Gakpo affording Alexander Isak a tap-in. The Dutchman is scarcely a right winger and faces an uncertain future at the end of the window. If Munoz had a fine introduction, this could prove Gakpo's goodbye, and his was a valiant effort.

An encouraging element for Liverpool is that Iraola has exerted an impact with his changes in each of his first two games. Munoz, who came on at St James' Park, swapped flanks at Anfield, took Florian Wirtz's pass, span and unleashed a vicious shot, even if a deflection off Murillo helped. It may not have been the first example of fine decision-making by Iraola: he pushed for Munoz's signing when Newcastle were closing in on his signature. "Victor has been very good both games," said Iraola. "Everything hasn't been perfect but he tries again and again and again and I like this from the wingers."

And so his tenure has begun with twin 2-2 draws. If it promises to be fun, at times his Liverpool can be both fast and flawed. Yet this underlined the size of his task if Iraola is to succeed his way. Liverpool had more defensive difficulties, with a susceptibility to the counter-attack again apparent, but with variations on a theme. Newcastle had scored twice by running straight through the heart of Iraola's team. Forest struck twice courtesy of balls in behind, the first punted 80 yards by goalkeeper Matz Sels; both involved throw-ins, too, the second a quick one by the debutant Liam Delap.

After the Forest striker added to the family tradition of Delap throw-ins, Alisson upended Neco Williams and Morgan Gibbs-White, an increasingly regular scourge of Liverpool, converted the resulting penalty. "It could and probably should have been a win," said Oliver Glasner. "Very proud of the performance but frustrated and disappointed about the result." So both new managers remain winless.

It looked a perfect storm for Liverpool; or maybe a Venn diagram of doom. Forest had won on their previous two trips to Anfield. Glasner had beaten Liverpool three times last season with Crystal Palace. Iraola tends to begin slowly in new jobs.

But they avoided the worst-case scenario and had a point to show for a rather mixed display. "The first half has been poor from our side," admitted Iraola, who drew more optimism from what followed.

Yet Liverpool again had a high defensive line and a susceptibility to counter-attacks. Glasner, despite his back-to-back losses to Leeds, seemed to be the new manager who had made the more immediate impact.

Liverpool were run ragged by Dan Ndoye and Igor Jesus. Gibbs-White showed there is life after Elliot Anderson for Forest. He played a part in both goals. For the opener, the Liverpool defence, attempting to push up, were caught out by Sels' long kick to Jesus, before Gibbs-White fed Ndoye to slot in. Alisson made a terrific save to deny Forest a second, tipping Jesus's shot on to the bar.

Wirtz had a goal disallowed when Jeremie Frimpong was offside. The German provided more promise than he had at Newcastle, drawing a fine save from Sels after a lovely Gakpo cross, finding the Dutchman in the build-up to the first equaliser and ending with an assist of his own. Isak, though, got his goal, just his second for Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

A subplot in a match where substitutions felt significant was that Iraola was readying a triple change, with Rio Ngumoha about to come on; the manager revealed that Gakpo would have been among those going off.

Instead, Glasner summoned Delap, fresh from his £45m club-record move from Chelsea. Iraola was aggrieved Liverpool were trying to make a triple change when the forward took the throw. "I wanted to make the subs about three minutes before," said Iraola. "I don't have an explanation." He suggested the fourth official's board was malfunctioning. So, though, was his defence.

They look in need of bolstering, though Liverpool are instead adding a winger for a nine-figure sum. Meanwhile, Glasner, set to sign Daniel Munoz and amid Forest interest in Harrison Armstrong, is eyeing more arrivals. "Definitely one, potentially two and probably three," he said. It could lead to departures. "Definitely one, potentially two and probably three," he grinned.

title: 'They are now athletes' - how do referees get ready for a season?
description: Pre-season camps in Spain and full-time training throughout the season - the rigorous regimes top-flight officials undergo to keep up with the pace of play in the Premier League
fullText:
Referees know every decision will be scrutinised.

Fans, pundits and players will pore over their calls, creating never-ending debates.

Many of the Professional Referee Group, the top officials in the country, have met in Loughborough this week.

They meet every few weeks to work and train together, with the officials spread across the country.

Lunch is a choice of chicken, teriyaki beef or tofu with vegetables and salad, with protein bars and rice cakes alongside the fruit, granola and Greek yogurts.

It is a reminder of the environment. Since becoming professional in 2001 top flight officials have had to adapt.

"I never thought referees did as much as what we do now," says Sam Allison, who played for Chippenham Town and Frome Town during his playing career, which started at Swindon.

"We are training full-time, sometimes two, three sessions a day, making sure that we are ready on a Saturday afternoon.

"Some of it (not understanding referees' workload) is probably ignorance, lack of awareness, lack of communication being disseminated to people out there.

"I think of my ignorance of just thinking referees just turned up, refereed the game and then went home.

"We have all the preparation, all the training, all the sacrifices, all the commitment, all the desire, all the support networks, people investing in you to make sure that you are ready in the best position to deliver a game."

Allison, a former firefighter, is the fourth official for Manchester City's trip to Crystal Palace on Friday while colleague Sam Barrott has been given Saturday's early match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.

Barrott took charge of Arsenal's Community Shield win over Manchester City this month and was in the Faroe Islands on 20 August to referee Ki Klaksvik's 0-0 draw with Riga in the Europa Conference League.

Different teams and different tactics means a different approach to each game, with officials prepping with Pro Ref's analysis team who provide key information to understand the way a team is going to play, to support the flow of the game.

It comes after a summer of work to ensure the officials can match - and better - the demands of the Premier League.

"At the moment we've got five substitutions and we see all the time fresh legs for teams can change the momentum in a game," said Barrott.

"If three new attacking players are on that are all very pacey after 70 minutes you know they're going to change the way they play, they're going to try and push.

"That normally means an increase in output for us and when that happens, there's not a point in us where we go, we can't handle this'.

"We've been trying to push the demands of where we are, everybody's trying to get better. Football has the 1% gains, every game or every training session we're very similar in the mindset, we want to be better."

Francis Bunce has been with Pro Ref - rebranded from the Professional Game Match Officials Limited - for 10 years and is now the physical performance manager.

He was with the group in Spain last month for their pre-season training camp, putting them through what is viewed as the infamous Maximal Aerobic Speed (MAS) test - an all out six-minute run.

"When you look at refereeing in the Premier League and Championship people very rarely talk about their physical qualities or physical capabilities," he tells BBC Sport.

"They've all done so well to keep developing and they look like athletes on the pitch - they are athletes.

"We're in a very different space with match officials, they are naturally some years older than the players and you can't get away from that because having a 21-year-old referee would be very difficult in the Premier League with everything you need to learn and experience.

"They should be definitely considered as athletes and if you then compare them to Joe Public who might want to shout some views from the sidelines, they wouldn't be able to keep up for a minute with what some of our guys can do."

With officials training remotely for part of the week, they need to be monitored with heart rate and GPS technology.

All the officials are on tailored plans and work in a group of around five once or twice a week at local hubs where strength and conditioning sessions are delivered.

Those at the World Cup - referees Michael Oliver and Anthony Taylor, along with assistants Gary Beswick, Adam Nunn, Stuart Burt and James Mainwaring - also had special training this summer, running and cycling in chambers of around 40 degrees to prepare them for the intense heat at the tournament.

Last season referees ran a total of 3.6m metres, with their overall sprint distance 12,136m.

At the weekend, Stuart Attwell covered the fourth highest distance of anyone on the pitch while taking charge of Newcastle's 2-2 draw with Liverpool, awarding the Reds a stoppage time penalty.

He was also fifth for highest high-speed running, therefore beating all but four players.

"A lot of people could go and run around the pitch but they wouldn't be able to pick up those key positions to make those defining decisions," says Bunce.

"That's something that's really important we build into our training, in terms of how we improve speed, how we improve being able to physically exert that kind of acceleration or high-speed running into a game.

"Then make a decision and to do it in a cool, calm manner and potentially have to make a VAR announcement and sound completely like they haven't been running around for 90 minutes."

The work pays off with Barrott recalling an incident in a match between Brighton and Fulham which underlined why it is worth it.

It came in March 2025 when he awarded a late penalty after Harrison Reed fouled Joao Pedro and the striker scored the injury-time penalty to earn the Seagulls a 2-1 win.

"I'm stood at the edge of the box, everyone turns and you're pointing at the penalty spot. There wasn't anything in me that thought 'you've got that wrong'," says Barrott.

"It was complete confidence, all because I'm stood in the right spot and to do that. It involves a little bit of football knowledge, anticipating what could happen and what we would call a danger area.

"But then also knowing what you've done for weeks and weeks - and potentially years and years - has allowed you to move into that position without having to think.

"It's just subconscious, it just happens and you're not stood there thinking: 'I'm tired, do I need to make that run?'

"That never comes into the thought process anymore, and the fatigue aspect of it never crosses your mind because we are where we need to be."

title: Departing Watkins apologised for refusing to play - Emery
description: Ollie Watkins is leaving Aston Villa as their record Premier League goalscorer.
fullText:
Manager Unai Emery said Ollie Watkins apologised for refusing to play for Aston Villa on Sunday as he paid an emotional tribute to the departing striker.

The 30-year-old is expected in Saudi Arabia on Friday to complete a £51m move to Al-Hilal, with Villa poised to finalise the signing of Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson for £65m as his replacement.

Emery praised the England forward's behaviour during his Villa career and said he and the squad had accepted Watkins' apology for making himself unavailable against Brighton.

Watkins is Villa's record Premier League scorer with 91 goals, part an overall tally of 108 in all competitions since signing from Brentford for £28m in 2020.

"He told us after the Brighton match he was sorry and that he had made a mistake. He was wrong, but we accepted it. The players as well," said Emery.

"His commitment and his behaviour was fantastic. He's a fantastic guy - a fantastic guy even more than a player. I told him 'bye' with a huge hug and with small tears.

"But now it's a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson."

Villa have agreed a deal for Jackson and are trying to ensure the Senegal striker is registered for Monday's visit of Arsenal.

Watkins is the latest experienced player to leave Villa this summer and Emery urged supporters to back the club's strategy despite the loss of several key figures in their successful 2025-26 season.

"We took decisions because it's good for the club," Emery said.

"Of course, we don't want to be a club that sells players, but the responsibility is there. It's crazy [money for someone] 30 years old and £50m for Ezri Konsa [who is 28].

"How we developed in the last year with some players and how we can sell some players now is completely the right decision.

"We have to rebuild the team as fast as possible. [Fans] have to accept our way and why we are taking some decisions."

As part of the rebuild, Leon Goretzka completed his move on a free transfer to Villa on Thursday after leaving Bayern Munich at the end of last season.

The midfielder won seven Bundesliga titles and the Champions League with Bayern.

"He is a winner. He is a very competitive player - a good player to add into our squad," said Emery.

"He is versatile and arrives fit and training well. Hopefully on Monday he can be on the field."

Ben is a lifelong Brighton fan who is feeling optimistic about the new season despite seeing more star players like striker Danny Welbeck and defender Jan Paul van Hecke leave the club this summer.

"We loved Danny, because he really fitted into our style of play and he had such a great season last year," Ben told BBC Sport.

"We will miss Van Hecke at the back too, but the thing with Brighton is that we always bounce back. We always come through with the players we bring in that I've never heard of, but they get given this chance.

"I just trust in [Brighton owner] Tony Bloom. He knows better than anyone about these things, because he has done it so many times before.

"He has sold so many world-class players to other clubs and we have nurtured so many great players to replace them.

"So, I don't feel there is any need to worry right now. Just put the trust in the club and see how we get on.

"It's great to be back in Europe [in the Europa Conference League] but with us potentially playing so many more games, I don't expect us to get there again through our league position this time.

"But my hope is that we won't drop into the bottom half of the table. My thinking is that, as long as we finish in the top 10 again and have a good go at Europe, then that's a great season."

Chris Sutton and Ben Thatcher were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

Crystal Palace had a poor start away to Everton and it looks like there's a bit of interest from Liverpool in Ismaila Sarr.

The one thing they can't do before the end of the window is lose all the best players. But I do think they've got a goal in them.

They didn't go big in the transfer window but they have got Liam Delap and he'll be hoping to get his career back on track. He had a disappointing season at Chelsea - which I know all about - but I do think there's a player in there and hopefully he'll he'll suit Forest.

It will be interesting to see who plays as that central striker. With the money they've spent on Delap then Chris Wood may not play a major role.

Last season he shot himself in the foot - forcing the move and then he had injury issues and it didn't quite happen for him. We know there's a player in there and for his sake and Liverpool's sake the sooner he comes to the fore the better.

What interested me against Fulham is Chelsea didn't have a lot of possession, but they were effective when they did have possession.

I really like Jack Hinshelwood he's such an exciting young player and there's a good history with his family in football and connection to Brighton.

But I'm going to say Chelsea carry on this run and get the three points.

Ben's prediction: I have to go with my team. It is going to be close - well, actually I don't know if it will be close... but I have just got to go with it. 1-2

Ben on which Brighton players will shine this season: We have managed to hang on to Bart Verbruggen, which was massive, and we have still got Georginio Rutter, who scored an amazing goal in pre-season against Roma, and then there is also Yasin Ayari.

But I've heard some amazing things about our Greek players Charalampos Kostoulas and Stefanos Tzimas, who we did not see much of last season. They will be like new signings for us.

Leeds and Daniel Farke proved loads of people wrong last season. But they were pretty cagey against Nottingham Forest last week in the Premier League.

They weren't very creative but then they got the job done against them in the EFL Cup in midweek and because of that I can't see Leeds losing.

Brentford are off to an absolute flyer - smashing Tottenham then hitting Birmingham for six or seven. They've started well with all the talk about their new midfielder Mamadou Sangare who now looks a bargain.

I think this is going to be really tight because Brentford like to play on the counter-attack.

Ben's prediction: This will definitely be close. 0-1

Sunderland need to get points on the board because they had a superb transfer window last summer but they've barely brought anybody in this year and their squad is going to be stretched because of Europe.

I got Sunderland really badly wrong last season but there's a lot of talk that they could be in trouble this year with so many games.

I still think they're good enough to stay up - they've got Granit Xhaka and some other good players. I like that they are physical and aggressive.

They made careless mistakes losing to Ipswich last week, giving the goals away, but I'm going to back Sunderland at home.

I think Fulham are going to be in a bit of bother this season, albeit they had some good spells against Chelsea last time out.

Ben's prediction: Sunderland's home crowd will lift them again - look how strong they were at the Stadium of Light last season. 2-0

Well done to Ipswich for their start. It took them 11 games to get the first win under Kieran McKenna the last time they were in the Premier League and they've got off to a great start already.

Under Gary O'Neil they have got a bit about them - they've got players who can get them up the pitch, they have got pace with Daizen Maeda and Emersonn looks a bit of a handful.

I think they could cause United one or two problems but it's unthinkable that Manchester United could lose their opening two games of the season. Their start was an absolute stinker - they were very flat against Hull.

With respect, it was an open goal start for the season for them, with Hull then Ipswich - two promoted sides - and it would be bordering on catastrophic for Michael Carrick if they lose again.

I remember the days when United used to beat Ipswich 9-0 but I don't think it will be nine and I think Ipswich will score. I think Ipswich will score first but United will come from behind to win - panic over, Carrick's the king again.

Ben's prediction: As much as I'd like to say Ipswich will win this, they won't. 2-0

There's only one winner with this.

I'm a massive fan of Unai Emery but the Ollie Watkins thing sickens you a bit, he was really let down by his striker last week.

Aston Villa had a slow start last season, they have lost big players and I just think Arsenal are going to run all over teams this season.

Physically the will be too strong and they played some good stuff against Coventry. I think they are going to get better and better which is ominous for everybody else.

I wouldn't totally rule Emery and Villa out of it because you just don't know. They're very principled in the way they play, probably the most principled team in the Premier League in the way that they build from the back.

But I think Arsenal will swarm all over them.

Ben's prediction: Arsenal to take it, just about. 1-2

title: Man City and Aston Villa to face holders PSG in Champions League
description: European champions Paris St-Germain will face Premier League duo Manchester City and Aston Villa in the league phase of this season's Champions League.
fullText:
European champions Paris St-Germain will face Premier League duo Manchester City and Aston Villa as well as five-time winners Barcelona in the league phase of this season's Champions League.

The back-to-back Champions League winners will welcome Barca to Parc des Princes, while they were also handed trips to Villa Park and Manchester in the draw for the league phase.

Premier League champions Arsenal, meanwhile, will host 15-time winners Real Madrid at Emirates Stadium, and have also been handed a trip to Bayern Munich.

Mikel Arteta's men, who were beaten by PSG on penalties in the final last season, will face Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis, Lille, Napoli, Azerbaijan champions Sabah and Slavia Prague as well.

Enzo Maresca's City will welcome PSG to Etihad Stadium and travel to Barcelona, where they will have a reunion with Spanish World Cup-winner Rodri, who moved to the Nou Camp in a £65m deal this summer.

City will also be up against another of their former midfielders in Kevin de Bruyne when Napoli visit Manchester, with Sporting, Porto, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and Lens their other opponents.

Europa League winners Villa, returning to the competition after a season away, will host PSG and Dortmund and travel to Barcelona and Galatasaray.

Unai Emery's side also face Club Brugge, Fenerbahce, Viking and Slavia Prague.

Manchester United, returning after a two-year hiatus, will meet Bayern, Atletico Madrid, Roma, Sporting, Leipzig, Villarreal, Sabah and Como.

Liverpool, meanwhile, host Atletico, Porto, Villarreal and Lens while visiting Inter Milan, Brugge, Fenerbahce and LASK.

The first league-phase matches will be played on Tuesday, 8 September and the last round of games will take place on 27 January 2027, with the exact schedule to be released on Saturday.

This season's final will be held in Madrid on 5 June.

Arsenal: Real Madrid (home), Bayern Munich (away), Borussia Dortmund (home), Real Betis (away), Lille (home), Napoli (away), Sabah (home), Slavia Prague (away)

Aston Villa: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Borussia Dortmund (home), Club Brugge (away), Fenerbahce (home), Galatasaray (away), Viking (home), Slavia Prague (away)

Liverpool: Atletico Madrid (home), Inter Milan (away), Porto (home), Club Brugge (away), Villarreal (home), Fenerbahce (away), Lens (home), LASK (away)

Manchester City: PSG (home), Barcelona (away), Sporting Club (home), Porto (away), Napoli (home), Leipzig (away), AEK Athens (home), Lens (away)

Manchester United: Bayern Munich (home), Atletico Madrid (away), Roma (home), Sporting Club (away), Leipzig (home), Villarreal (away), Sabah (home), Como (away)

Each of the 36 teams plays eight different teams - four at home and four away - in the league phase.

Teams who finish in the top eight automatically qualify for the last 16, while those placing ninth to 24th will compete in a two-legged knockout play-off for the chance to join them.

Sides who finish 25th or lower will be eliminated, and will not drop into the Europa League.

Last season, eventual runners-up Arsenal topped the league phase standings with 24 points after eight wins from as many matches.

Liverpool were third - behind second-placed Bayern Munich - with 18 points while Tottenham finished one point behind in fourth.

Chelsea and Manchester City also qualified directly for the last 16 after finishing sixth and eighth respectively while Newcastle finished 12th.

Chelsea, Manchester City, Newcastle and Spurs were knocked out in the last 16 last season while Liverpool were beaten in the quarter-finals by PSG, who also edged Arsenal in the final for their second consecutive title.

title: Fan backlash as gay World Cup star joins Saudi club
description: Spain forward Esther Gonzalez attracts backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
fullText:
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.

The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.

Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".

However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.

Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.

Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.

According to Spanish outlet El Mundo,, external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.

Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.

The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.

The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.

Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.

Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.

Gotham FC declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

title: Will a Premier League club break record for transfer sales in one window?
description: Aston Villa, Manchester City and Newcastle are closing in on Monaco's record for transfer income generated in a single window.
fullText:
Premier League clubs are usually associated with spending heavily in the transfer market, but this summer several have been making as much noise through their sales.

Aston Villa, Manchester City and Newcastle United have already moved into the all-time top six for transfer income generated in a single window, with Monaco's 360m euros haul from 2018-19 now within reach.

Monaco's record was built around several major departures, most notably Kylian Mbappe's 180m euros move to Paris St-Germain, while Thomas Lemar joined Atletico Madrid for 72m euros and Fabinho moved to Liverpool for 45m euros.

On 26 August, according to Transfermarkt, which lists transfer fees in euros, Villa have brought in 293.1m euros (£251m) from departures this summer, City 278.6m euros and Newcastle 275.5m euros.

Only Monaco, Chelsea's 321m euros in 2025-26 and Atletico Madrid's 314m euros in 2019-20 currently sit above them.

And with several days of the window still remaining, the record could yet fall.

Villa are currently closest to Monaco with Morgan Rogers' £117m (138m euros) move to Chelsea accounting for a significant chunk of their total. Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne were also among those to leave.

Their summer trading has also left them with the strongest positive transfer balance in the Premier League.

Villa have spent 160.5m euros, which leaves them 132.6m euros in profit on transfer dealings. That activity comes against a backdrop of financial pressure.

In June, Villa were fined 22.5m euros by Uefa for a significant breach of its squad-cost rule for 2025, with 15m euros of that amount suspended on the condition that the club continued to reduce its squad-cost ratio during 2026.

The impact of losing several senior players was evident on the opening weekend, when Unai Emery's side suffered a 4-0 defeat by Brighton.

Speaking afterwards, Gary Neville said Villa looked as though they had had their "heart ripped out", pointing to the experience lost through the departures of Rogers, Tielemans and Konsa.

Villa could yet move even closer to the record.

Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal have made several attempts to sign Ollie Watkins, with Villa reportedly rejecting an offer worth around 52m euros. Emery has already acknowledged that the England striker could leave, although the two clubs remain apart on valuation.

Manchester City's position has shifted following Wednesday's signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi. They have generated 278.5m euros from sales so far, with the departures of players including Savio, Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Manuel Akanji and Nathan Ake.

Bouaddi's arrival takes City's spending to 273.7m euros, leaving them with a positive transfer balance of 4.8m euros.

Further departures could quickly change the picture again. Tottenham have agreed a loan deal to sign Omar Marmoush, with an obligation to make the move permanent for £60m (58m euros) next summer. That fee would therefore count towards City's 2027-28 transfer income rather than this season's figures.

Nico Gonzalez is also expected to leave, while Jack Grealish could yet be another departure before the deadline. Grealish spent last season on loan at Everton, who remain interested, although the winger has viewed Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola as manager as a fresh start at City. His contract runs until June 2027.

A permanent sale of Gonzalez, and possibly Grealish, could still significantly increase City's 2026-27 income.

Their ability to sell at such a level is particularly significant given the scale of their midfield rebuild. City have already signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for 135m euros. They also remain interested in Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

Newcastle have reached 275.5m euros in sales with the bulk of that coming from three major departures.

Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for 108m euros, Bruno Guimaraes moved to Arsenal for 87.5m euros and Anthony Gordon signed for Barcelona for 80m euros.

Together, those deals have transformed Newcastle's summer balance sheet.

They have spent 197m euros, which leaves them 78.5m euros in profit.

Only Villa and Nottingham Forest currently have a larger positive transfer balance among Premier League clubs.

The volume of sales across the division is reflected in the wider transfer balances.

Six Premier League clubs currently have a positive balance, according to Transfermarkt:

At the other end of the scale, Chelsea have the largest negative balance at 242.3m euros after spending 407.95m euros and receiving 165.65m euros.

Tottenham are next at 189.15m euros in the red, followed by Arsenal at 180.95m euros with several days until the transfer window closes on 1 September.

Brighton's sales figures illustrate a different approach.

Over the past five seasons, Brighton have spent 665.4m euros on players and received 715.4m euros in transfer fees, leaving them with a positive transfer balance of about 50m euros.

According to Transfermarkt, they are the only current Premier League club to have made a cumulative transfer profit across that five-season period. Aston Villa are the next closest to break-even, with an overall balance of -10.02m euros.

That underlines how consistently Brighton have combined significant player sales with reinvestment, rather than relying on one unusually profitable window.
